meta.note: Starting points only. The real subject of this site is the circle a student draws, anywhere in the country.

startingPoints.name: The Mississippi Delta
startingPoints.invitation: A river that moved cotton, blues music, and floodwater — and is still moving all three.
startingPoints.look: Levees, oxbow lakes, cypress, and farmland that used to be swamp.

startingPoints.name: The Everglades
startingPoints.invitation: A river sixty miles wide and six inches deep, drained and half re-flooded within one lifetime.
startingPoints.look: Sawgrass to the horizon, hardwood hammocks, and canals cut straight as rulers.

startingPoints.name: The Sonoran Desert
startingPoints.invitation: One of the most biodiverse deserts on earth, and one of the fastest-warming cities in the country.
startingPoints.look: Saguaro, ocotillo, dry washes that flood in minutes, mountains on every side.

startingPoints.name: The Great Smoky Mountains
startingPoints.invitation: More salamander species than anywhere else on the planet, in mountains people were removed from to make a park.
startingPoints.look: Fog in the coves, old-growth stands, rhododendron thickets, cold streams.

startingPoints.name: Puget Sound
startingPoints.invitation: Salmon, orcas, ports, and dams — a food web and a shipping lane sharing the same water.
startingPoints.look: Douglas fir, tide flats, ferry wakes, mountains behind the skyline.

startingPoints.name: The Chesapeake Bay
startingPoints.invitation: The largest estuary in the country, fed by farm runoff from six states and worked by watermen for centuries.
startingPoints.look: Marsh grass, crab pots, eroding islands, blue herons on every dock.

startingPoints.name: The Flint Hills Prairie
startingPoints.invitation: The last large piece of tallgrass prairie left — ninety-six percent of it is gone.
startingPoints.look: Grass over your head in August, burned black in April, limestone under everything.

startingPoints.name: The Great Lakes Dunes
startingPoints.invitation: Freshwater so big it makes weather, with dunes piled four hundred feet above it.
startingPoints.look: Beech-maple forest, perched dunes, water that turns turquoise over sandbars.

startingPoints.name: The Yukon River Basin
startingPoints.invitation: Ground that has stayed frozen for millennia is thawing, and the salmon runs are arriving at the wrong time.
startingPoints.look: Black spruce leaning at angles, braided rivers, thaw ponds, twenty-one hours of June light.

startingPoints.name: The Lower Rio Grande Valley
startingPoints.invitation: Birds from two continents funnel through here, across a river that is also a border with a wall on it.
startingPoints.look: Thorn scrub, resacas, citrus groves, and species found nowhere else in the country.

sections.title: The place
sections.lead: Put your reader inside the circle you drew. Write like you are describing it to someone who has never been.
prompts: Where is this circle, and why did you put it there?
What does it look like — hills, water, trees, fields, buildings, roads?
What would you hear and smell standing in the middle of it?
Who spends time here — and when are they here?

sections.title: Who lives here
sections.lead: Pick two or three of the species you collected and introduce them. Read their Wikipedia entry first — it is right there on each species card.
prompts: What is it, in your own words? Say it the way you would to a friend.
Where in your circle would you actually run into it — a tree, the water, the sky, under a rock?
Have you ever seen one? If yes, describe it. If no, what did you picture before you looked it up?
Which one surprised you most, and what surprised you about it?

sections.title: What I still want to find out
sections.lead: End with a question instead of a conclusion. Good writing usually does.
prompts: What is the one thing you most want to know about this place now?
What could you do to find out — look something up, ask someone, go and stand there?
What would you go outside and check tomorrow?
What did you believe about this place before today that you are less sure of now?
